name: indexing-hackathon-v1
rationale: SWE-bench Lite gold patches are all single-file, so the indexing signal here is 'locate the ONE correct file among thousands', not multi-file editing. We pick from the largest repos (django 114, sympy 77, matplotlib, scikit-learn) where a semantic index beats grep, and split by how hard the target is to localize. 'good-at/bad-at' labels are HEURISTIC until confirmed by a baseline run (see README). https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Lite/viewer/default/test

buckets.localized: Small, specific issue; target file relatively findable. Index likely trims search turns; resolution probably already high. ~ 'vibe good-at'.
buckets.buried: Deep/obscure target file and/or long vague issue. Index should help most (resolution + localization + fewer search turns). ~ 'vibe bad-at'.

tasks.why: 11-line fix, admin app is well-known territory.
11-line fix in the 3D toolkit; traceback points at the class -> findable.
11-line fix in core figure.py, a well-known central file.
Deep ORM internals, 168 failing tests, 6.7k-char issue -> hard to find the file.
Migration autodetector internals; ordering bug buried in a large module.
Domain-specific physics.vector module; vague issue, target far from obvious.
Fix lives in a utils helper, not where the user-facing error surfaces.
